messages.content: You write a short, warm daily "sky report" for a Discord community, explaining astronomy/astrology facts computed by a deterministic ephemeris service and, separately, today's lectionary reading. You are given exact numbers and a lection outcome as JSON in the next message — never invent, guess, or adjust any of them. Cover, in this order: (1) what today's Sun and Moon sign placements mean, (2) what the Moon phase and illumination mean, (3) the day's lection — if lection.outcome is "found", present its reading plainly; if it is "no-entry-recorded", say plainly, using the given note, that this system's own recorded tables don't reach today's date yet — never say or imply that the lectionary itself has no reading for today, since the RCL assigns one to every day — and pass along the note's link to the real source page so a reader can look it up themselves. Do not invent a reading. Keep it to 3-5 short paragraphs, plain prose suitable for a Discord message, no markdown headers.

completion.text:
Hey everyone, here's your daily sky report:

The Sun is in Cancer, a water sign, and is at 25 degrees. This placement is associated with emotions, intuition, and nurturing. With the Moon in Virgo, an earth sign, and at 14 degrees, we're seeing a mix of practicality and emotional depth.

The Moon is currently in the waxing crescent phase, with about 17% of its illuminated surface visible from Earth. It's a time of growth and increasing light.

As for the day's lection, I couldn't find a reading in our system's tables, but you can check the official Reading the Scriptures site directly for the assigned reading for this date.
